faq.title: Answers before the first call.
faq.text: The questions teams ask most, answered without the sales detour.

items.q: Why should my marketing team care about Astro instead of a traditional page builder like WordPress or Webflow?
items.a: Astro ships almost no JavaScript by default, so pages load fast and score well on Core Web Vitals. For marketing teams, that means better rankings, lower bounce rates, and higher conversion rates from the same traffic. You get the speed of a hand-coded site without giving up flexibility.

items.q: Will my team still be able to edit content without a developer?
items.a: Yes. Astro pairs with headless CMS options like Sanity, Contentful or Storyblok. Your team edits copy, images, and landing pages in a familiar interface, and the site rebuilds automatically. Developers are only needed for new components or structural changes.

items.q: How does Astro help with SEO and AI search visibility (AEO)?
items.a: Astro renders clean, fully static HTML that search engines and AI crawlers can read instantly, with no client-side rendering delays. Combined with structured data, semantic markup, and well-organized content, your pages are far more likely to be indexed, cited in AI answers, and surfaced in featured snippets.

items.q: Will I lose my SEO rankings when I leave Webflow or Wordpress?
items.a: Not if the migration is done properly. I keep your URL structure, set up 301 redirects wherever URLs change, and carry over meta tags, schema, and sitemaps. I also monitor indexing and rankings after launch to catch any issues early. In many cases, performance improves after the move.

items.q: How long does an Astro website project take?
items.a: A typical marketing site takes 3 to 4 weeks, depending on the number of pages, custom components, and CMS complexity. A focused landing page or microsite can be live in 1 to 2 weeks. I share a clear timeline upfront, with milestones you can review along the way.

items.q: Can Astro integrate with our existing marketing stack?
items.a: Absolutely. Astro works with Google Analytics, GTM, HubSpot, Segment, Meta Pixel, Hotjar, and most A/B testing tools. I set up tracking and event measurement during the build, so your campaigns are measurable from day one.

items.q: Is Astro suitable for large or growing sites?
items.a: Yes. Astro handles anything from a five-page brand site to thousands of content pages, including blogs, docs, and programmatic SEO pages. Because pages are pre-built and served from a CDN, performance stays consistent as traffic and content scale.

items.q: What happens after launch? Do you offer ongoing support?
items.a: Yes. I offer maintenance and iterative optimization after launch, from monthly Core Web Vitals audits to new landing pages and A/B test support. You’re never left with a site nobody understands.

items.q: How much do Astro development services cost compared to other options?
items.a: Pricing depends on scope, but Astro projects often cost less to run over time: hosting is cheap or free, there are no plugin licenses, and maintenance overhead is low. I provide a fixed-scope quote after a short discovery call, so there are no surprises.

faq.q: Why do you price by templates instead of pages?
faq.a: Because templates are where the work is. Fifty pages built on five layouts take less time than ten pages with ten unique layouts. Content moves with scripts, so a blog with 300 posts costs the same as one with 30.

faq.q: What if my site does not fit a package?
faq.a: Most sites land in one of them. If yours sits between two, the audit tells us which, and you get a fixed quote before anything starts. If it needs more, it goes into Protocol and gets scoped line by line.

faq.q: Why Astro?
faq.a: Astro ships almost no JavaScript by default, so pages paint fast on a phone without a fight.

faq.q: Will my Google rankings drop after the migration?
faq.a: Not when the redirect map holds. I keep every URL that earns traffic at the same path, diff the old and new sitemaps before the switch, and watch Search Console through the first month.

faq.q: Can my marketing team still publish without a developer?
faq.a: Yes. We agree on the editing path, a headless CMS or structured content files, before I write the first component. Publishing without a ticket is a requirement, not an extra.

faq.q: Do I own the code?
faq.a: Yes. The repository, the hosting, and the CMS sit on your accounts from day one. Nothing on the site needs me around to keep running.

faq.q: What does hosting cost after I leave Webflow?
faq.a: For most marketing sites, close to nothing. A static Astro site runs on the free or entry tiers of Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare. A headless CMS can add a monthly fee, and I list it in the quote so there are no surprises.

servicePages.painTitle: What a slow site actually costs you.

pain.title: You pay twice for every visitor.
pain.text: Ads and content bring someone to the page, then a four second paint sends them back to the search results. You paid for that click and got nothing for it.

pain.title: Google ranks the wait.
pain.text: Core Web Vitals are a ranking signal. A failing largest contentful paint holds a page down no matter how good the copy on it is.

pain.title: The desktop score is not the problem.
pain.text: A green number on a desktop test means little when your buyer is on a mid range Android over 4G. That is the device I test on.

works.title: The critical path
works.text: Render blocking scripts and stylesheets come out of the head, fonts get preloaded and metric matched, and the browser paints text on the first pass instead of the third.

works.title: The JavaScript you ship and never run
works.text: Most sites download a whole framework to animate three sections. I cut what is dead, defer what can wait, and load the rest only where it earns its bytes.

works.title: Media that holds the paint hostage
works.text: Hero images get sized, converted, and served at the width the layout actually asks for. Video that autoplays above the fold stops blocking the first frame.

works.title: Layout shift
works.text: Everything that arrives late gets its space reserved before it lands — images, embeds, and the font swap that quietly drops your headline one line down the page.

servicePages.proofText: The same tests, run before and after, with the raw reports attached. Median mobile PageSpeed across the last five projects is 97, up from 35, and largest contentful paint went from 4.1s to 1.2s on a throttled Moto G4.

faq.q: How fast can you make my site?
faq.a: Most sites I take on land above 90 on mobile. What I promise before the audit is the measurement, not a number: I profile the site first, tell you what each fix is worth, and you decide how far down the list to go.

faq.q: Will you break my design?
faq.a: No. Speed work is plumbing — the page looks the same and arrives sooner. Anything that would change a layout goes on a staging URL for you to review before it ships.

faq.q: What if my platform is the bottleneck?
faq.a: Then I tell you. Every builder has a ceiling, and I know where it sits: what to cut, what to move out of the head, and the point where the honest answer is a rebuild in Astro rather than another round of tuning.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: A typical pass runs one to two weeks from audit to shipped, depending on how much of the site is custom and how quickly your review comes back.

servicePages.ctaText: I run the audit and reply within a day with what I would fix first and what it is worth.

servicePages.metaDescription: I structure your pages so ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews quote you by name instead of a competitor — and I measure it on the same prompts.
servicePages.subtitle: Ask a model about your own category and it lists three competitors. I structure your pages so the answer comes out of yours, with your name attached.
servicePages.painTitle: Why the answer names someone else.

pain.title: The click is disappearing.
pain.text: Your buyer asks a model instead of typing a query, reads the answer it gives, and never sees the ten blue links you optimised for.

pain.title: Models quote what they can parse.
pain.text: A page built out of nested divs and text baked into images gives a model nothing to lift. Structure, a clear question, and a direct answer give it a paragraph to quote.

pain.title: You cannot win a question you never answer.
pain.text: Most sites describe a product. An answer engine is looking for the sentence that answers the question your buyer actually asked, in the words they asked it.

works.title: Structured data that matches the page
works.text: Organization, Person, Service, FAQPage and breadcrumbs, wired into one entity graph so a crawler knows what the company is and who stands behind it, instead of nine disconnected blobs.

works.title: Answers written to be lifted
works.text: The question goes in a heading and the answer goes in the first two sentences under it. No preamble for a model to wade through before it reaches the part worth quoting.

works.title: Crawlable to the machines that matter
works.text: A robots.txt that lets GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot in, a sitemap that stays current on its own, and content that renders in HTML rather than after a JavaScript bundle.

works.title: Entity signals off the page
works.text: The profiles, mentions and links that tell a search engine which company owns your name. Most AEO packages skip this part, and it is the part that decides whether you show up at all.

servicePages.proofTitle: How you tell whether it worked.
servicePages.proofText: I record the answers first: the same prompts, in the same models, before anything changes. After the work we run them again and you see where your name now appears and where it still does not. No agency dashboard, just the transcripts.

faq.q: What is AEO and how is it different from SEO?
faq.a: SEO earns a link in a list. AEO earns a sentence inside the answer. The work overlaps — both want a fast, crawlable, well structured page — but AEO optimises for being quoted rather than being clicked.

faq.q: Can you guarantee ChatGPT will mention me?
faq.a: No, and anyone who guarantees it is selling you something. Models change and none of them publishes a ranking. What I can do is remove every reason a model has to skip you, then measure the difference on the same prompts.

faq.q: Does AEO work hurt my Google rankings?
faq.a: The opposite. Structured data, fast pages and clear answers are what classic SEO has asked for all along. AEO is that same work, aimed at a reader that happens to be a model.

faq.q: How long does it take to see results?
faq.a: Technical fixes and structured data can be picked up within weeks, while building lasting authority and citations usually takes a few months. Timelines vary by industry, competition, and how much content needs work, and I’ll give you a realistic outlook after the audit.

faq.q: Does site speed and performance affect AEO?
faq.a: Yes. Fast, clean, well-structured pages are easier for crawlers to access and process, and they give users a better experience too. That’s why I combine AEO with web performance optimization instead of treating them separately.

faq.q: Will AEO work for a Web3 or fintech company?
faq.a: Yes, and these industries benefit a lot from it. Buyers in Web3 and fintech research heavily and often ask AI tools to explain products, compare options, and assess credibility. Clear, accurate, trustworthy content helps you show up in those conversations, while staying within the compliance expectations of your industry.

faq.q: How do I get started?
faq.a: Book a call and I’ll review your current site, see how AI tools currently talk about your brand, and outline a clear plan with priorities and next steps.

works.title: A repository your team recognises
works.text: Astro, plain components, and no framework tax you did not ask for. Pages ship as finished HTML, and JavaScript loads only where a section actually needs it. It builds on Vercel or wherever you host today.

works.title: Content stays editable

servicePages.proofText: A Git repository with the full history, a build that runs on your own hosting, the redirect map, and the speed reports before and after. No part of the site needs me around to keep it running.

faq.q: Will the site look different?
faq.a: No, unless you want it to. The default is a faithful rebuild: same design, same content, same URLs, new foundation underneath.

faq.q: What do you rebuild it in?
faq.a: Astro. It serves finished HTML with almost no JavaScript, which is why the rebuild lands faster than the site it replaces, and it is plain enough that any engineer you hire later can pick it up.

faq.q: Can marketing still publish without a developer?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a requirement rather than an extra. We agree on the editing path — a headless CMS or structured content files — before I write the first component.

faq.q: Will I lose my SEO rankings when I leave Webflow?
faq.a: Not if the migration is done properly. I keep your URL structure, set up 301 redirects wherever URLs change, and carry over meta tags, schema, and sitemaps. I also monitor indexing and rankings after launch to catch any issues early. In many cases, performance improves after the move.

faq.q: What happens to my CMS content and blog posts?
faq.a: I export your CMS collections and migrate them to the new setup, whether that’s a headless CMS, a database, or a code-based content system. Your posts, images, and metadata move over intact, and your team gets an editing experience that suits your workflow.

faq.q: Will there be any downtime during the migration?
faq.a: No. I build and test everything on a staging environment, then switch over at the DNS level once everything is verified. That keeps downtime close to zero.

faq.q: What about my forms, integrations, and third-party tools?
faq.a: I rebuild and reconnect your forms, analytics, CRM, email tools, and any other integrations, then test each one before launch so no leads or data get lost.

servicePages.ctaText: I reply within a day with what the rebuild involves and where the platform is actually costing you.
